info.description:
AList V4 HTTP API. All endpoints return the common envelope
`{"code": int, "message": string, "data": T}`; a `code` of 200 means success.
Authenticated endpoints require the `Authorization` header set to the access
token returned by `/api/auth/login` (or `/api/auth/login/hash`).
Base URL is `conf.URL.Path` (empty by default) followed by `/api`, e.g. `/api/me`.

reviewed_version.description:
ReviewedVersion is the plugin version whose declared permission set this
Grant was approved against (design §6.2 reviewed_version). Update compares
the new version's requests against it to decide whether re-consent is due.

license.description:
Provenance fields (Step 11). The official index lists OPEN-SOURCE plugins
only; FetchIndex drops any entry that is closed-source or paid. Proprietary/
paid plugins are installed only by URL/file, where the trust-tier gate
forces them through the 🔴 risk path.

source.description:
Source is the name of the plugin source this entry came from ("official"
or an imported source's name). Set by AggregateIndex, not by the index
file itself.

config.description:
Config is the persisted config_form values an admin set for this plugin
(a JSON object). Stage 1: stored/served for the admin UI only — the plugin
cannot yet read it back (the reverse host bridge is a later wave). Empty
until an admin saves.

grant.description:
Grant is what the admin APPROVED for this plugin (design §6.2), persisted
alongside the rest of the lifecycle state. It — not the Manifest — is the
runtime authority: the dispatch gate and the borrowed-capability layer read
it, so a capability the Manifest declares but the Grant omits is denied. Nil
until consent is recorded; a nil Grant means default-deny at the gate, NOT
"fall back to the Manifest". A direct install records a default Grant
(grantFromManifest); a wizard/consent install or a post-install adjust
overwrites it via SetGrant.

name.description: manifest i18n display name (LangMap); shown by the UI instead of the id

needs_reconsent.description:
NeedsReconsent marks a plugin whose active version requests MORE than the
current Grant approves (design §6.6, set by Update). The extra capabilities
stay denied at runtime until the admin re-approves via SetGrant; the UI
surfaces the flag so the admin knows re-consent is due.

answers.description:
Answers carries the current step's own recorded answer (e.g. the oauth
step's exchanged token, once HandleOAuthCallback has completed it) so a
polling caller can pick it up without waiting for Done. Done responses
carry every step's merged answers instead (the full config, credentials
included, for the caller to use when creating the resulting storage).

auth_url.description:
AuthURL is set when the current step is an oauth step awaiting
authorization: the frontend opens it (e.g. in a popup) and waits for the
provider to redirect the browser to the host's oauth callback (WS-8).

config_sections.description:
ConfigSections render titled setting groups on a feature's config page
(design C). A base feature declares its own "general" section with
Parent=self; an extension whose config extends a base feature declares one
with Parent=<base feature id>. The frontend's FeatureConfigPage(id) collects
every section (across enabled extensions) whose Parent==id.

file_columns.description:
FileColumns add a badge/column to the file listing (design §4): the labels
badge. Its data source is the extension's FileDecorator field group.

login_methods.description:
LoginMethods render login affordances for an AuthNMethod (design §4):
primary/federated login-page buttons, or a second-factor prompt component.

public_pages.description:
PublicPages render an extension's unauthenticated landing page (design §4):
a share bundle's public page (iframe, guest context).

public_prefix.description:
PublicPrefix is the top-level short URL prefix an extension requests for
its PublicPages (design §3 PublicRouter): a share bundle requesting "/s"
is reachable at "/s/:share_id" instead of the default
/api/v4/ext-public/{id}/... namespace. A single, rooted, lowercase
alphanumeric-plus-hyphen segment (e.g. "/s") — validated at manifest load
(ValidateManifest) for that shape, and at registration
(Registry.RegisterPluginMode/Register) against the reserved-word table
(internal/extension/apiroute.go CheckReservedPrefix) and cross-plugin
mutual exclusion (a second extension requesting an already-claimed
prefix is refused). Empty means no custom prefix: the extension's
PublicPages stay under the default namespace.

status_providers.description:
StatusProviders render a runtime status card the host polls (design §4):
AccessProtocol / BackgroundService plugins (running state, port, metrics,
start/stop toggle).

x-depends-on.description:
DependsOn / Assist are the SDK §4.1 extension keywords. The host carries
them verbatim to the frontend (page-zero assist); it does not act on them.

x-secret.description:
Secret marks this property as holding a credential (G3 §1: secret as a
first-class citizen, step 1 — declare + read-back sentinel only, no
encryption yet). A plugin's config_form uses this to mark a
GetPluginConfig/SetPluginConfig field the host must never echo back in
full once saved — the storage-driver Additional-item equivalent is the
existing Type=="password" convention (ext.Item has no such flag of its
own; a storage driver's fields go through driver.Item.Secret instead,
derived from Type=="password" for a plugin driver or the
`confidential:"true"` Go struct tag for a built-in one — see
internal/extension/info.go). x-secret follows the same x- extension-key
style as x-depends-on/x-assist above; the host carries it verbatim to
the frontend and also reads it itself to redact GetPluginConfig's
response and to preserve a stored value when SetPluginConfig receives a
blank resubmission.

detail.description: Detail is an optional human-readable line (last error, current phase).

metrics.description:
Metrics is optional free-form structured telemetry for the status card
(e.g. {"proxies":3,"traffic_bytes":10485760}).

state.description: State is the coarse lifecycle state: "running" | "stopped" | "error".

poll_path.description:
PollPath is the host status endpoint the frontend polls, e.g.
"/api/v4/extensions/{id}/status/{ID}" → the host resolves the extension's
Status().

css.description: optional relative path to the restricted CSS (§5.4)

tokens.description: relative path to the token JSON (spec §5.3)

provider.description:
Provider is the AuthProvider extension id an oauth step drives (WS-8).
Required when Type == WizardOAuth; the host resolves it to a live
ext.AuthProvider and calls AuthURL/Exchange against it — locally, never
through an external broker.

scopes.description: Scopes are the OAuth scopes requested from Provider. oauth only.

mode.description:
Mode is "outbound" (default) or "reverse" (design R4). ReverseAddr is the
dialable WS URL, meaningful only in reverse mode.

reverse_status.description:
ReverseStatus is the live reverse-connection status the server's reverse
supervisor tracks for this agent (connected/dialing/error + last-seen over
the channel). Nil for an outbound agent, or a reverse agent the supervisor
is not yet tracking.

rapid.description:
Rapid is true only when the task is done AND completed via hash-based
rapid-upload ("秒传", design SP-H): the agent reports the shared
proto.RapidUploadDetail marker as the done-status detail. We surface
only this boolean, never the raw detail string, so a done detail that
ever carried some other value can't leak through this field.

src.description: Src doubles as the task's display name (its source path).

disable_warning.description:
DisableWarning is the declarative disable-consequence copy (Manifest.
DisableWarning, i18n LangMap). When non-empty the frontend shows a
"are you sure?" confirm carrying this message before disabling — replacing
the old hardcoded CONFIRM_ON_DISABLE_IDS set. Absent for the common case
where disabling has no special consequence.

include_secrets_key.description: carry the shared secrets key (storage/plugin secret encryption) so it can decrypt on restore to a different machine; requires password

password.description: when set, domain payloads are AES-256-GCM encrypted

sanitize.description: strip storage credentials / user secrets (mutually exclusive with password)

fields.description:
Fields/Pending carry extension field-group decorations for the listed page
(design §2.6), present only when the request asked for fields. Fields maps
group → ref key (ext.RefKey, the object's virtual path) → column value;
Pending lists the groups whose decorator exceeded its budget, to be
backfilled via /fs/fields.

Fields requests extension field groups (comma-separated, "_"-prefixed, e.g.
"_labels,_shares") for the listed page (design §2.6). Base fields always
return; a requested group is computed on demand by its FileDecorator under a
per-group budget, and a group that exceeds the budget is returned in Pending
for the client to backfill via /fs/fields. Empty means no decoration.

remember.description:
Remember, if set, issues a longer-lived refresh token (see
common.RefreshTokenRememberFactor) instead of the default refresh TTL.

Remember, if set, issues a longer-lived refresh token — mirrors
LoginReq.Remember (this replaces the login the password step parked).

copy_perms.description:
CopyPerms applies to copy only: clone the source subtree's manual
permissions onto the destination. Default false.

perm_policy.description:
PermPolicy applies to move only (spec 0-C): "" / "follow" (default) keeps
manual permissions following the object; "detach" drops them from the
moved subtree.

server_pubkey.description:
ServerPubKey is this server's own ed25519 public key (base64), from the
identity boot loaded via agentsrv.CurrentServerIdentity (design R1). The
agent PINS it for a later reverse-connection wave (R2), where the server
signs its handshake and the agent verifies against this pinned key — the
mirror image of the server verifying an agent's heartbeat signature. A
public key is not a secret, so returning it on this anonymous endpoint
is safe; the pairing SAS already guarantees it was pinned without a MITM.
Empty (omitted) when no server identity was wired at boot — the pairing
still succeeds, the agent simply has nothing to pin this wave.

response.description:
Response is the raw navigator.credentials.create() result JSON, passed
through verbatim to the WebAuthn engine.

acknowledged.description:
Acknowledged confirms the admin accepts the risk of granting the plugin
network hosts BEYOND what its manifest declared. Required (true) whenever
the submitted grant's network set contains a host the manifest did not
request; ignored otherwise. Only network may exceed the manifest.

grant.description:
Grant is the admin-approved consent selection to record for the plugin
(design §6.4 consent submit). Optional: when omitted, install records the
default Grant (approve the manifest's requests). A wizard-driven install
submits the admin's actual selection here so the runtime authority reflects
exactly what was approved, not what the manifest declared.

value.description: Value is base64-encoded, since a KV value is opaque bytes.

ttl.description: TTL is in seconds; <= 0 or omitted lets Signer apply its own default/cap.

perm_policy.description:
PermPolicy: "" / "follow" (default) keeps manual permissions following the
renamed object; "detach" drops them from the renamed subtree (spec 0-C).

reveal.description:
Reveal opts into storing the token in plaintext (readable back via
GetToken). Defaults to false: the token is stored as a salted,
irreversible hash (see conf.TokenPlaintext / pkg/utils.HashToken) and
only ever returned in the response of this call.

mode.description:
Mode / ReverseAddr configure reverse-connection mode (design R4). Mode
must be "outbound" or "reverse"; when the RESULTING mode is reverse the
resulting ReverseAddr must be a well-formed ws/wss URL, else the PATCH is
rejected — a reverse agent with no dialable address is never persisted.

language.description:
Language is the user's explicit locale preference (e.g. "zh-CN"). Empty
means "follow the request's Accept-Language". Added in migration 0006.

permission.description:
Permission is the legacy 17-bit mask. The column is kept for the
baseline-frozen schema (same treatment as Authn); all runtime reads
were retired in v4 Step 5 — authorization is RBAC5 (op.Authorize).

permission_entries.description:
PermissionEntries is the typed view (fs + system) built from
op.UserPermissions; unknown actions pass through opaque (spec §9).

permissions.description:
Permissions is the legacy int32-bitmask view kept for the running
frontend; it cannot represent system-domain grants. Retire once the
frontend migrates to PermissionEntries (Phase 5.2).

concurrency.description: for accelerating request, use multi-thread downloading

node_id.description:
NodeID references the nodes table (v4 permission stage 1): the directory's
stable identity, from which the live virtual path is derived (meta
resolution matches on that derived path). 0 means unanchored — above every
mount point, or a migration row not yet adopted — and then the Path is the
truth. Path is always populated (it is the meta's nodeless fallback
identity); for a node-anchored row it is a stale display value that the
meta index overrides with the derived path. Path carries only a plain index
(not unique): a stale stored Path left behind by a move must not block
reclaiming that path — meta uniqueness is enforced in op on the LIVE derived
path (op.ensureMetaPathFree), never on the stored column.

display_name.description:
DisplayName is a purely cosmetic label for admin-authored permissions
(front-end display only; never consulted by the authorization engine).
Left empty for built-in/scope-origin rows, which are identified by Name.

node_id.description:
NodeID references the nodes table (v4 permission stage 1): the object's
stable identity, from which the live virtual path is derived (the fs
engine matches on that derived path, never the stored Path). 0 means
unanchored, and only then is Path the truth: system-domain rows (Path is
the domain selector), scope declarations, above-mount virtual paths, and
migration rows not yet adopted. A node-anchored fs row stores no Path.

resource_type.description:
ResourceType selects the matching domain: "fs" (or "") targets a
filesystem virtual Path; "system" targets an admin control-plane domain
(Path holds the domain selector). Type is a security-load-bearing gate:
a row of one type never satisfies a decision of the other.

permission_scopes.description: PermissionScopes stores structured permission list and is ignored by gorm.

protected.description:
Protected marks built-in roles (admin/guest and future presets) that the
role API must refuse to rename or delete.

group.description: use to group setting in frontend

addition.description: Additional information, defined in the corresponding driver

Language is the user's explicit locale preference (e.g. "zh-CN"). Empty
means "follow the request's Accept-Language". Added in migration 0006.

permission.description:
Permission is the legacy 17-bit mask. The column is kept for the
baseline-frozen schema (same treatment as Authn); all runtime reads
were retired in v4 Step 5 — authorization is RBAC5 (op.Authorize).

authenticatorAttachment.description:
AuthenticatorAttachment If this member is present, eligible authenticators are filtered to only
authenticators attached with the specified AuthenticatorAttachment enum.

requireResidentKey.description:
RequireResidentKey this member describes the Relying Party's requirements regarding resident
credentials. If the parameter is set to true, the authenticator MUST create a client-side-resident
public key credential source when creating a public key credential.

residentKey.description:
ResidentKey this member describes the Relying Party's requirements regarding resident
credentials per Webauthn Level 2.

userVerification.description:
UserVerification This member describes the Relying Party's requirements regarding user verification for
the create() operation. Eligible authenticators are filtered to only those capable of satisfying this
requirement.

id.description: CredentialID The ID of a credential to allow/disallow.

transports.description: The authenticator transports that can be used.

id.description: A unique identifier for the Relying Party entity, which sets the RP ID.

name.description:
A human-palatable name for the entity. Its function depends on what the PublicKeyCredentialEntity represents:

When inherited by PublicKeyCredentialRpEntity it is a human-palatable identifier for the Relying Party,
